page: Microsoft Azure FX24-12mds_v2 is a specialized virtual machine configuration providing high per-core performance paired with an exceptionally large memory allocation. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance provides 12 dedicated vCPUs derived from 6 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 processor architecture includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) alongside AVX-512 vector extensions. With 504 GB of RAM, the system maintains a 42 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio.

Local ephemeral storage is provided via a bundled 1416 GB NVMe SSD, avoiding external network storage overhead for temporary working sets, cache layers, or scratch data. No discrete GPU hardware is included. Benchmark measurements show top-tier single-core compute performance, recording a Geekbench single-core score of 2356.0 and text processing scores of 3012.0. Single-threaded data throughput is reinforced by strong compression benchmarks, achieving 34.85 GB/sec in gzip compression and 14.47 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression.

Multi-core execution and uncached memory operations register within average industry bands, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 11836.0 and 93.22 GB/sec uncached large-block read bandwidth. While prompt processing and lightweight 135M model generation perform competitively, larger model text generation drops significantly, reflecting the 12-thread constraint and absence of GPU acceleration. In-memory operations achieve 18.95 million Redis SET operations per second.

Cost efficiency is centered on high memory capacity and high CPU clock speed per licensed core, making it well suited for software constrained by per-core licensing fees. The architecture is primarily configured for large in-memory databases, electronic design automation (EDA), relational databases requiring high memory-to-core ratios, and data transformation pipelines that require fast local NVMe staging.
description: Microsoft Azure FX24-12mds_v2 is a memory-dense, high-frequency compute instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The virtual machine provides 12 dedicated vCPUs across 6 physical cores on the x86_64 architecture, supported by a 260 MB L3 cache, AVX-512, and AMX instruction sets. With 504 GB of system memory, the instance delivers an exceptional 42 GB of RAM per vCPU, complemented by an integrated 1416 GB NVMe SSD for fast local ephemeral storage. Hardware benchmarks reflect top-tier single-thread performance, leading to strong throughput in compression and text processing workloads, while multi-threaded compute remains bounded by the 12-vCPU count. Lacking GPU acceleration, this instance is configured specifically for memory-intensive enterprise software, high-performance in-memory databases, EDA simulation tooling, and workloads where per-core software licensing benefits from high clock speeds combined with extensive RAM allocations.
